resources.string: Boox Notes’ instant pen preview, lent to other apps

In Boox Notes, ink appears under the pen tip at once because the screen draws it directly instead of waiting for the app. Instant ink does the same while one of the apps you choose is open: a preview stroke appears the moment the pen touches, and the app’s own strokes replace it when you pause. The app isn’t changed and still receives every pen movement.

Android tells an app which app is open only if you allow usage access. Without it, Instant ink never switches on. Tap Allow usage access, find BooxUltimatum in the list and turn it on. If the switch won’t turn on, allow it from a computer with adb: adb shell appops set app.booxultimatum GET_USAGE_STATS allow
Connected through Shizuku, because the display didn’t answer BooxUltimatum directly

If preview ink stays on the screen, Recover screen stops the pen preview, undoes the other display changes it can leave behind and repaints everything. Clean screen flashes the whole screen once to clear ghosting.
Pen preview stopped and screen repainted

Pencil draws a steady line exactly as wide as the width you set. Fountain pen follows your pressure like the pen in Boox Notes and can draw up to 3 px wider than the width. Brush pen swells with pressure, up to twice the width. Grainy pencil is Boox’s black speckled texture, for apps whose pencil or charcoal has grain. It darkens as you press, broadens as you tilt the pen and draws about 5 px wider than the width.

While you write, the display holds back the app’s own drawing, so quick strokes share one preview, as in Boox Notes. When the pen has rested this long after a lift, or leaves the screen, the app’s strokes appear in its own brush and colour. A shorter pause shows them sooner. A longer pause keeps quick writing on the preview. Boox’s own screen notes offer the same choice, from 400 ms to 2 s.

The preview is Boox’s own brush in black, not the app’s brush, colour or eraser. Those appear when the app’s strokes take over, once you pause or as soon as the pen leaves the screen. Grainy pencil is textured and can look broken at small widths, so Fountain pen is the default. The preview pauses while the pen’s eraser end is near and while the screen is off or locked, and it resumes when the tip comes near.\nInstant ink needs usage access, a permission you can grant on the tablet, so it knows which app is open. It shows a small notification while it runs, so Android doesn’t stop it behind your drawing app. Turn off or Recover screen ends it at once.

Turning Instant ink off from your drawing app

The Instant ink notification has the only Turn off and Recover screen buttons you can use outside BooxUltimatum. Android hides it because notifications aren’t allowed for BooxUltimatum. Allow notifications to show the buttons again. Instant ink posts no other notification.

Without leaving your drawing app, the Instant ink tile in Quick Settings turns it on or off, and the buttons on its notification turn it off or recover the screen. The Clean screen tile flashes the whole screen as soon as you close Quick Settings.
